questions.prompt: You're writing a triangle scene. One character speaks; the other two listen differently. Which craft moves stack to make the scene work?

options.label: Pick a voice register the speaker keeps consistent + write a line whose subtext lands differently on each listener + give the branch a real consequence.
Make the dialogue louder and more dramatic for each character.
Have every character say the same thing in different ways.

questions.mentorPostScript: Voice + subtext + branch — all three at once is where dialogue craft lives.

questions.prompt: You wrote a 12-node tree with two branches. The voice scores are strong, the subtext is layered, but the tag balance shows one character used 'said' eleven times. What does the synthesis-level revision look like?

options.label: Replace several 'said' tags with action beats — the rhythm of the scene gets unstuck without losing voice.
Add more lines for that character so the ratio drops.
Delete the character's lines so the imbalance disappears.

questions.mentorPostScript: Synthesis revision moves one axis without breaking the others. Action beats fix tag balance without touching voice.

questions.prompt: A branch point is meaningful when…

options.label: The two paths cost the speaker something different, and the next line of dialogue genuinely changes based on which path the kid picks.
Both paths lead back to the same line eventually.
One path is the 'right answer' and the other is wrong.

questions.mentorPostScript: Real branches diverge. Cosmetic branches converge. Pick the kind that actually changes the scene.

questions.prompt: You're scoring a tree across voice / subtext / tag balance / branch. Three axes are strong, one is weak. The honest revision move is…

options.label: Spot which axis is weakest and fix THAT — not the ones already working. The strong axes don't need help.
Rewrite the whole tree from scratch.
Ignore the weak axis — three out of four is good enough.

questions.mentorPostScript: Find the weakest axis. Patch it. The strong axes don't need your time.

questions.prompt: Patter calls a published tree 'a conversation.' Why is that word load-bearing for the craft?

options.label: Because a conversation has voices that respond to each other — not a paragraph one person delivers. Every line in the tree is one half of a back-and-forth.
Because conversations are easier to grade than essays.

questions.mentorPostScript: Write a conversation, not a paragraph. Voices respond. That's the whole game.
